units.text: It reads and writes Excel files in the XLSX format. It creates, edits, and formats spreadsheets using classes such as Workbook, Worksheet, and Cell. It supports data validation and conditional formatting rules.

It creates, loads, and saves Excel workbooks through the Workbook class, manages individual worksheets via a WorksheetCollection, and provides access to cell data through a Cells collection that supports string, numeric, boolean, date/time, and formula values.

It reads and writes cell values including formulas, supports setting and retrieving cell content types, and preserves formula expressions and error values such as #N/A, #VALUE!, and #REF! during load and save operations.
It applies full cell styling through the Style class, including font properties, borders, fills, alignment, and custom number formats, and adjusts row heights and column widths explicitly.

It enforces data validation rules on cell ranges using Validation with types such as whole number and operators like between, and applies conditional formatting to highlight cells based on value conditions.

It embeds images from bytes, streams, or file paths with two-cell anchor positioning, supports cell comments with author, text, visibility, and size controls, and manages drawing shapes with preset geometries.
It creates and manipulates charts and structured Excel tables, including support for various chart types and table features such as column definitions and totals rows.

This example creates a new workbook, names the first worksheet Report, writes a text value and a number into cells A1 and B1, applies bold formatting and a custom number format to the number, adjusts row height and column width, and saves the result as report.xlsx.

Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java supports data validation and conditional formatting rules. The following example creates a validation range and applies a conditional format to highlight values between 1 and 100.
Create a validation range and apply conditional formatting to highlight values between 1 and 100.
The public entry point is org.aspose.cells_foss. The classes below cover the full supported public API surface — 183 public types organized into one module.
The org.aspose.cells_foss package serves as the primary namespace for the Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java library, providing access to workbook, worksheet, and cell manipulation capabilities.
It adds additional spreadsheet save formats beyond .xlsx, a full formula calculation engine, ChartEx chart type creation, and dedicated enterprise support.
